text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Swedish state-owned telecoms company Telia is to be 49 percent privatised in 1998. The company is valued at around 40 billion Swedish crowns.
--Danes in February spent almost one billion crowns more on holidays abroad than foreign tourists spent in Denmark.
--Family-owned Danish business Foss Electric has become the world's leading producer of analytical instruments for the food industry with its purchase of Sweden's Perstorp Analytic.

--A.P. Moeller can be happy about the billion-crown increase in its annual accounts. It was mainly due to increased North Sea oil production and a rise in oil prices. It also increased oil production in Qatar and made a profit on its international oil business for the first time.
--The long-awaited industrial upturn is still not here. New data from the National Statistics Office shows that seasonally-adjusted production fell by one percent month-on-month in January.
--With 1.3 billion crowns in venture capital the Danish Growth Fund has created 800 new jobs, many of them in the IT field.

--Sophus Berendsen on Thursday presented annual accounts showing a net result, excluding minorities, of 911 million crowns, a five percent fall compared to the previous year. CEO Hans Werdelin's salary is reduced by 3.3 million crowns to 4.7 million, as a result of Berendsen's bonus system.
--Danish unemployment fell to 8.1 percent in February, from 8.2 percent the month before, partly because there were 1,400 more people on paid leave schemes.

--The Confederation of Danish Industries fears that the government will use fiscal policy to dampen domestic private demand, for example by introducing punitive rates of interest to discourage borrowing by variable-rate loans.
